mainTopic: ספר הישר, the sun standing still for יהושע and משה, שאול's portion, and the start of the משנה's rule on יחוד with גוים
overview: The גמרא asks what ספר הישר is, since a פסוק in יהושע says the sun standing still is 'written' there. רבי יוחנן says it is בראשית, the book of the אבות, and finds the hint in יעקב's blessing to אפרים. Three אמוראים then argue, in two versions, about how many hours the sun stood still: 24, 36 or 48. A ברייתא adds that the sun also stood still for משה and for נקדימון בן גוריון. The גמרא finds a source for משה in three different ways, and answers the challenge that יהושע's day was 'like no other'. A second פסוק about teaching בני יהודה the bow also mentions ספר הישר. רבי יוחנן, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמואל בר נחמני identify that book as בראשית, דברים or שופטים, and each finds a hint to the bow. The same three then explain which part of the animal was served to שאול with the thigh. Finally the גמרא returns to the משנה's ban on a woman being alone with גוים and starts asking what case it means.

steps.title: What is ספר הישר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the sun standing still for יהושע, which mentions ספר הישר, and asks what that book is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation avenged itself of its enemies. Is it not written in the book of Yashar?' What is the book of Yashar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק from ספר יהושע and asks what 'ספר הישר' means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק refers to a book called ספר הישר as if we should know it. The גמרא wants to identify which book this is, since no book in תנ״ך has that name.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of Yashar (the book of the upright), mentioned in the פסוק

phrases.english: "And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed,
until the nation avenged itself of its enemies.

phrases.aramaic: הֲלֹא הִיא כְתוּבָה עַל סֵפֶר הַיָּשָׁר״,
phrases.english: Is it not written in the book of Yashar?"
What is the book of Yashar?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which book the פסוק means by ספר הישר.

steps.title: It is the book of the אבות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ספר הישר is the book of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, who are called 'ישרים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the book of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, who are called 'upright', as it says: 'Let my soul die the death of the upright.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that ספר הישר is the book about the אבות, meaning ספר בראשית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from a word match: the אבות are called 'ישרים' in a פסוק in במדבר. So 'the book of the ישר' means the book that tells the story of those ישרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Upright people, a name for the אבות
As it is said (introducing a פסוק)
Let my soul die the death of the upright

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the book of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
phrases.notes: He means ספר בראשית, the book that tells their story.

phrases.english: who were called "upright,"
as it says: "Let my soul die the death of the upright."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ספר הישר is ספר בראשית, the book of the אבות, who are called ישרים.

steps.title: Where is it hinted in בראשית?
steps.stepSummary: If the event is 'written' in ספר בראשית, where is it hinted there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up: if the sun standing still is 'written' in בראשית, where is it? This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer of step 2 creates a problem: בראשית never openly tells about יהושע. So the גמרא looks for a hint (רמז) in בראשית.

phrases.english: And where is it hinted?
phrases.notes: Where in בראשית is the sun standing still for יהושע hinted at?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the answer of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The place in בראשית that hints at the sun standing still for יהושע.

steps.title: The hint in יעקב's blessing to אפרים
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'his seed will be the fullness of the nations' refers to the time the sun stood still for יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And his seed will be the fullness of the nations.' When will he be the fullness of the nations? At the time when the sun stood still for יהושע: 'And the sun stood in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set, about a whole day.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds the hint in יעקב's blessing to אפרים: his descendant would fill the nations, which happened when the sun stood still for יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע came from אפרים. When the sun stood still for him, his fame spread to all the nations of the world, so this is when 'his seed filled the nations'.

phrases.english: "And his seed will be the fullness of the nations."
phrases.notes: בראשית 48:19, יעקב's blessing to אפרים, the tribe יהושע came from.

phrases.english: When will he be the fullness of the nations?
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the words in square brackets; they belong to the corrected wording.

phrases.english: At the time when the sun stood still for Yehoshua,
"And the sun stood in the middle of the sky
and did not hurry to set, about a whole day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blessing that אפרים's seed would fill the nations came true when the sun stood still for יהושע.
steps.whatToRemember: ספר הישר is ספר בראשית, and the hint there to the sun standing still is יעקב's blessing to אפרים.

steps.title: How long did the sun stand still?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how many hours the sun stayed in the sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how long the sun stayed in the sky that day. This sets up three different answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק just quoted says 'about a whole day', which is not exact. The גמרא now wants to know the actual number of hours.

phrases.english: And how long?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the words 'about a whole day' from the פסוק in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The number of hours the sun stayed in the sky.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: twenty-four hours
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the whole event lasted 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Twenty-four hours. It moved six and stood six, moved six and stood six; the whole thing was like a full day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the whole day lasted 24 hours: the sun moved for six hours, stopped for six, moved for six, and stopped for six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, 'about a whole day' describes the total event: 6+6+6+6 equals 24 hours, one full day. So the sun stood still for 12 hours in total.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Twenty-four [hours]:
it moved six and stood six,
it moved six and stood six,
the whole thing was like a full day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The whole event lasted 24 hours; 'a whole day' refers to the entire event.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: thirty-six hours
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says it lasted 36 hours, with the standing still alone adding up to a full day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Thirty-six. It moved six and stood twelve, moved six and stood twelve; its standing still was like a full day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר says the day lasted 36 hours: the sun moved six hours, stopped twelve, moved six, and stopped twelve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'about a whole day' as describing only the time the sun stood still: 12+12 equals 24. Add the 12 hours it moved, and you get 36.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Thirty-six:
it moved six and stood twelve,
it moved six and stood twelve,
its standing still was like a full day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהושע בן לוי in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The event lasted 36 hours; 'a whole day' refers only to the time the sun stood still.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: forty-eight hours
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says it lasted 48 hours, and proves from the wording of the פסוק that the second stop was longer than the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: Forty-eight. It moved six and stood twelve, moved six and stood twenty-four, as it says: 'and did not hurry to set, about a whole day.' This implies that at first it was not a whole day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the day lasted 48 hours: six moving, twelve stopped, six moving, then twenty-four stopped. He brings a proof from the order of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first says 'the sun stood in the middle of the sky' and only later 'about a whole day'. He learns that the first stop was less than a full day (12 hours) and the second stop was a full day (24 hours).

keyTerms.meaning: By implication, from this we learn

steps.confusionAlert: All three אמוראים agree the sun moved for a total of 12 hours. They only argue about how long it stood still: 12, 24, or 36 hours.
steps.whatToRemember: 24 hours (רבי יהושע בן לוי), 36 hours (רבי אלעזר), or 48 hours (רבי שמואל בר נחמני). Each reads the words 'about a whole day' differently.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
Forty-eight:
it moved six and stood twelve,
it moved six and stood twenty-four,
as it says: "and did not hurry to set, about a whole day."
This implies that at first it was not a whole day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion that gives the second stop a full 24 hours, with a proof from the order of the פסוק quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The event lasted 48 hours: a 12-hour stop and then a 24-hour stop, proven from the wording 'about a whole day' appearing only at the end of the פסוק.

steps.title: Second version: the argument is about the extra hours, starting with רבי יהושע בן לוי
steps.stepSummary: Some say the מחלוקת is only about the added time. In this version רבי יהושע בן לוי says 24 extra hours were added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say they argue about the extra time. רבי יהושע בן לוי says 24 hours were added: the sun moved 6 hours and stood 12, then moved 6 hours and stood 12. So its total standing time equaled a full day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same argument. In this version the argument is only about how much time was ADDED to the day, and it opens with רבי יהושע בן לוי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, 24 hours was the length of the whole event. Here, 24 hours is only the extra time: two stops of 12 hours each. The phrase 'its standing was like a full day' shows where the 24 comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: The addition: here, the extra hours added to the day
Its standing (the time the sun stood still)

steps.confusionAlert: Here תוספתא is not the book called תוספתא. It simply means 'the addition', the extra hours added to that day.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
they argue about the added time:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמַר: עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבְּעָה —
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: twenty-four.
It went six and stood twelve,
it went six and stood twelve,
so its standing equaled a full day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the three-way מחלוקת from steps 6-8 in a second version that counts only the added hours.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 24 extra hours were added: two stops of 12 hours each.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר in the second version: 36 extra hours
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says 36 hours were added: one stop of 12 hours and a second stop of 24 hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says 36: the sun moved 6 hours and stood 12, then moved 6 hours and stood 24, as it says 'and it did not hurry to set for a full day.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives his number for the extra time, 36 hours, and supports it with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'a full day' as describing only the second stop, so that stop alone was 24 hours. Add the first stop of 12 hours and the total is 36.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: thirty-six.
It went six and stood twelve,
it went six and stood twenty-four,
as it says: "And it did not hurry to set for a full day."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second opinion within the second version of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 36 extra hours were added: stops of 12 hours and 24 hours.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני in the second version: 48 extra hours
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says 48 extra hours: two stops of 24 hours each. He bases this on comparing the sun's standing to its moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says 48: the sun moved 6 hours and stood 24, then moved 6 hours and stood 24. The פסוק compares its standing to its going: just as its going takes a full day, so too each standing lasted a full day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives the biggest number, 48 extra hours, and explains his reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the sun standing and the sun going together, so he compares them (היקש). A normal day of the sun's going is a full day, so each stop must also have been a full 24 hours. Two stops of 24 hours make 48.

keyTerms.meaning: Its going / moving across the sky
Just as ... so too: the form of a comparison

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version all three opinions count only the ADDED time: 24 (12+12), 36 (12+24), and 48 (24+24).

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: forty-eight.
It went six and stood twenty-four,
it went six and stood twenty-four.
The פסוק compares its standing to its going:
just as its going takes a full day,
so too its standing lasted a full day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: אַרְבָּעִים וּשְׁמוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and last opinion in the second version of the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 48 extra hours were added: two stops of 24 hours each, based on the היקש between standing and going.

steps.title: The sun also stood still for משה and for נקדימון בן גוריון
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the sun stood still not only for יהושע but also for משה and for נקדימון בן גוריון. For יהושע we know it from פסוקים, and for נקדימון from a tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: just as the sun stood still for יהושע, it also stood still for משה and for נקדימון בן גוריון. For יהושע we know it from פסוקים; for נקדימון בן גוריון we know it from a tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds two more people for whom the sun stood still. The גמרא then notes how we know about יהושע and about נקדימון, which sets up the question about משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only lists the three people. The גמרא then adds how we know about two of them: פסוקים for יהושע and a tradition for נקדימון. For משה there is no source yet, so the next step asks about it.
steps.confusionAlert: Here גמרא does not mean the Talmud. It means a tradition that was passed down, not a פסוק.

phrases.english: It was taught:
Just as the sun stood still for Yehoshua,
so too the sun stood still
for Moshe and for Nakdimon ben Guryon.
For Yehoshua, we know it from verses;
for Nakdimon ben Guryon, we know it from tradition.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁעָמְדָה לוֹ חַמָּה לִיהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how long the sun stood for יהושע to other times the sun stood still.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sun stood still for יהושע, משה, and נקדימון בן גוריון.

steps.title: How do we know it happened for משה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the sun stood still for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: For משה, how do we know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where we learn that the sun stood still for משה, since it has just given sources for יהושע and נקדימון but not for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע has פסוקים and נקדימון has a tradition, but no פסוק openly says the sun stood still for משה. So the גמרא asks for a source.

phrases.english: For Moshe, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the one case in step 12 that was left without a source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the sun stood still for משה.

steps.title: Learned from the word 'אחל' in both places
steps.stepSummary: The word 'אחל' (I will begin) appears about משה and about יהושע, so we link the two: what happened for יהושע also happened for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'אחל' and 'אחל'. About משה it says 'I will begin to put your dread,' and about יהושע it says 'I will begin to make you great.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word appears in a פסוק about משה and in a פסוק about יהושע, so the sun miracle is carried over to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ uses the word 'אחל' for both leaders. That shared word links the two, so the sun standing still, which we know about for יהושע, is also true for משה.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes / is learned from: introduces a גזירה שוה
A link made between two פסוקים because they share the same word

phrases.english: It is learned from "I will begin" and "I will begin":
phrases.notes: The same word shows up in two places, so the גמרא links them. This is called a גזירה שוה.

phrases.english: It is written here: "I will begin to put the dread of you,"
and it is written there about Yehoshua: "I will begin to make you great."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'אחל', found both about משה and about יהושע.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: learned from the word 'תת' instead
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן links משה and יהושע through the word 'תת' (to put/give). It appears about משה and in the פסוק about יהושע's battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says it is learned from 'תת' and 'תת'. About משה it says 'I will begin to put your dread,' and about יהושע it says 'on the day ה׳ gave over the אמורי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different word-link to show the sun stood still for משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both views agree that the source is a גזירה שוה from the same פסוק about משה. They differ only on which word makes the link. רבי יוחנן's פסוק about יהושע comes from the very place where the sun stood still, which makes for a direct link to that miracle.

keyTerms.meaning: The Amorites, the nation יהושע fought

steps.whatToRemember: The sun stood still for three people. For יהושע we know it from פסוקים, for נקדימון from a tradition, and for משה from a גזירה שוה, either on 'אחל' or, according to רבי יוחנן, on 'תת'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is learned from "to put" and "to put":
It is written here: "I will begin to put the dread of you,"

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב בִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ ״בְּיוֹם תֵּת ה׳ אֶת הָאֱמֹרִי״.
phrases.english: and it is written about Yehoshua: "On the day ה׳ gave over the Amorites."
phrases.notes: יהושע 10:12, the same פסוק where יהושע tells the sun to stand still.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different גזירה שוה from step 14 to answer the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'תת', linking the פסוק about משה to the פסוק about יהושע's battle.

steps.title: Proof straight from the verse that the sun stood still for משה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני learns that the sun stood still for משה from the plain wording of the פסוק in דברים, with no word-link needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: You can learn it from the verse itself: 'who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you.' When did the nations tremble and shake because of you? At the time the sun stood still for משה.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third answer to the question of Step 13 (where do we see the sun stood still for משה). רבי שמואל בר נחמני does not need a word-link at all, because he reads it right out of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two earlier answers linked משה and יהושע through a shared word ('אחל' or 'תת'). Here the proof comes from the content of the פסוק. It promises that the whole world will tremble at משה, and such worldwide fear fits a sight the whole world could see: the sun standing still.

keyTerms.meaning: From the verse itself, meaning from its own wording and not from a link to another verse
They trembled and were in anguish

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
You can learn it from the verse itself:
"who shall hear the report of you,
and shall tremble and be in anguish because of you."
When did they "tremble and be in anguish because of you"?
At the time when the sun stood still for Moshe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר, מִגּוּפֵיהּ דִּקְרָא שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, different source for the same fact that Steps 14 and 15 proved through word-links
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The promise in דברים 2:25 that the nations would tremble at משה came true when the sun stood still for him.

steps.title: Challenge: there was never a day like יהושע's day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the פסוק says no day before or after was like יהושע's day, so how could the sun also have stood still for משה?
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: 'And there was no day like that, before it or after it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that the sun stood still for משה too. A פסוק in יהושע says that day was one of a kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sun had already stood still for משה, then יהושע's day would not be unique. Since the פסוק says 'before it', meaning no earlier day was like it, it seems to deny that this happened for משה.

phrases.english: They challenged this:
"And there was no day like that, before it or after it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the claim proved in Steps 14 to 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the sun stood still for משה, and also for נקדימון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A day that was 'like no day before or after' cannot be the same kind of miracle that already happened for משה.

steps.title: First answer: משה's miracle lasted fewer hours
steps.stepSummary: The sun did stand still for משה, but not for as many hours as it did for יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: it was the hours that were not as many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer to the challenge. יהושע's day was unique in how long the sun stood still.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps the miracle for משה but makes it smaller. The uniqueness in the פסוק is about the length of the miracle, not about whether the sun stopped at all.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say; it brings one possible answer, often followed by another

phrases.english: If you want, say:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁעוֹת הוּא דְּלָא הֲווֹ (נפיש) [נְפִישָׁן] כּוּלֵּי הַאי,
phrases.english: it was the hours that were not as many as this.
phrases.notes: Some versions read נפיש, others נְפִישָׁן (the square-bracket wording). Both mean 'many'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing what 'no day like it' refers to: its length
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No day before or after had the sun stand still at all
steps.terutzMaskana: The sun stood still for משה, but for fewer hours than for יהושע

steps.title: Second answer: משה's day had no hailstones
steps.stepSummary: Another way: יהושע's day was unique because hailstones fell from heaven, which did not happen for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: there were no hailstones, as it is written: 'And it came to pass, as they fled from before the children of Israel, while they were on the descent of בית חורון, that ה׳ cast great stones from heaven on them, as far as עזקה, and they died.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer. What made יהושע's day like no other was the hailstones, and it proves that they fell with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer allows the miracle for משה to be just as long. The uniqueness of יהושע's day is a different, extra miracle that happened on that same day: great stones falling from heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: בית חורון, the slope where the enemies fled
עזקה, a place the stones fell as far as

steps.whatToRemember: The sun stood still for משה too. יהושע's day is still 'like no other' because it lasted longer, or because hailstones also fell.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
there were no hailstones,
phrases.notes: He means there were none in the time of משה.

phrases.english: as it is written:
"And it came to pass, as they fled from before the children of Israel,
while they were on the descent of Beit Choron,

phrases.aramaic: וַה׳ הִשְׁלִיךְ עֲלֵיהֶם אֲבָנִים גְּדֹלוֹת מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם
phrases.english: that ה׳ cast great stones from heaven upon them
as far as Azeikah, and they died."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אַבְנֵי בָרָד לָא הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to an extra miracle that made the day unique
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the sun standing still could make the day unique
steps.terutzMaskana: The hailstones made יהושע's day unique, so the sun can still have stood still for משה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge is answered in two ways, and the claim that the sun stood still for משה stays in place.

steps.title: What is ספר הישר in the פסוק about the bow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק in שמואל ב about teaching בני יהודה the bow, 'written in ספר הישר', and asks what that book is.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And he said: To teach the sons of יהודה the bow; behold, it is written in ספר הישר.' What is ספר הישר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another פסוק that mentions ספר הישר and asks which book it means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר הישר was mentioned earlier in this sugya about יהושע's battle. Now it shows up again in a פסוק about דוד teaching בני יהודה to use the bow, so the גמרא asks to identify the book.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of the upright (ספר הישר)

phrases.english: It is written: "And he said: To teach the sons of Yehudah the bow;
behold, it is written in the book of Yashar."
What is "the book of Yashar"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about a different פסוק that mentions ספר הישר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which book is called ספר הישר

steps.title: It is the book of the אבות, who are called 'ישרים'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says ספר הישר is the book of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, since a פסוק calls them 'ישרים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: This is the book of אברהם, יצחק and יעקב, who are called 'upright', as it is written about them: 'Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: ספר הישר is the book about the אבות, meaning ספר בראשית. It proves that the אבות are called 'ישרים' from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name 'ישר' matches the word 'ישרים' that בלעם uses for the אבות. So 'the book of the ישר' means the book that tells the story of the ישרים.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
This is the book of Avraham, Yitzchak and Yaakov,
who are called "upright ones,"
as it is written about them:
"Let my soul die the death of the upright,
and let my end be like his."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: זֶה סֵפֶר אַבְרָהָם יִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ספר הישר is the book of the אבות, who are called ישרים

steps.title: Where in that book is the bow hinted at?
steps.stepSummary: If ספר הישר is בראשית, the גמרא asks where it hints at teaching בני יהודה the bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it hinted at?
steps.whatsHappening: The פסוק said the bow for בני יהודה 'is written in ספר הישר', so the גמרא asks where. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ספר הישר is identified as the book of the אבות, the claim in שמואל ב has to be found there. Nothing in בראשית openly speaks about a bow for יהודה, so the גמרא looks for a hint.

phrases.english: And where is it hinted at?
phrases.notes: Where in the book of the אבות is teaching יהודה the bow hinted at?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the answer of Step 21 and asks for the actual place in that book
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The place in בראשית that hints at יהודה using the bow

steps.title: יעקב's blessing to יהודה hints at the bow
steps.stepSummary: יעקב tells יהודה, 'your hand on the back of your enemies' neck'. The only kind of fighting where the hand is by the back of the neck is archery.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'יהודה, your brothers shall praise you; your hand shall be on the back of your enemies' neck.' And which kind of warfare needs the hand to be opposite the back of the neck? You must say: this is the bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with יעקב's ברכה to יהודה and explains why it hints at the bow. This completes רבי יוחנן's view; the next steps bring two other opinions on what ספר הישר is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'your hand on the back of the neck' describe a hand held near the neck in battle. The גמרא says this fits shooting a bow, so the bow for בני יהודה really is 'written in ספר הישר', which is בראשית.

keyTerms.meaning: The back of the neck, the nape
You must say; it shows the only possible answer

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, ספר הישר is בראשית, the book of the אבות. Its hint for teaching יהודה the bow is 'your hand on the back of your enemies' neck', which describes archery.

phrases.english: "Yehudah, you, your brothers shall praise you;
your hand shall be on the back of your enemies' neck."
And which is the kind of warfare
that needs the hand to be opposite the back of the neck?
You must say: this is the bow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא מִלְחָמָה שֶׁצְּרִיכָה יָד כְּנֶגֶד עוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בראשית 49:8, 'your hand on the back of your enemies' neck', hints at the bow
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוחנן, the phrase 'written in ספר הישר' in שמואל ב points to יעקב's ברכה to יהודה in בראשית.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: ספר הישר is משנה תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says ספר הישר is משנה תורה (ספר דברים), because that book commands us to do 'הישר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: ספר הישר is the book of משנה תורה. Why is it called 'the book of the upright'? Because it says there: 'And you shall do what is upright and good in the eyes of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion about what ספר הישר is. רבי אלעזר says it is ספר דברים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן linked the name 'ישר' to the אבות, who are called 'ישרים'. רבי אלעזר links the same name to a פסוק in דברים that uses the word 'הישר'. Next he must still show where דברים hints at teaching the bow.

keyTerms.meaning: ספר דברים, the fifth book of the תורה

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: זֶה סֵפֶר מִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: this is the book of Deuteronomy,
phrases.notes: He means ספר הישר, the book named in the פסוק from שמואל ב.

phrases.english: and why did they call it 'the book of the upright'?
As it is written: 'And you shall do what is upright and good in the eyes of the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: זֶה סֵפֶר מִשְׁנֵה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 20, disagreeing with רבי יוחנן's answer in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספר הישר is ספר דברים, called 'ישר' because of the פסוק 'ועשית הישר והטוב'.

steps.title: Where does דברים hint at the bow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where ספר דברים hints at teaching בני יהודה the bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests רבי אלעזר's view. If ספר הישר is דברים, where does דברים talk about teaching the bow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמואל ב says the teaching of the bow is 'written in ספר הישר'. So any book suggested as ספר הישר must contain some hint to this. This is the same test the גמרא gave רבי יוחנן's view in step 22.

phrases.english: And where is it hinted?
phrases.notes: He means: where in דברים is there a hint to teaching בני יהודה the bow?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source in דברים that would back up רבי אלעזר's claim.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A hint in ספר דברים to teaching בני יהודה the bow.

steps.title: 'His hands shall contend for him' means the bow
steps.stepSummary: In משה's ברכה to יהודה it says 'ידיו רב לו', his hands (plural) fight for him. The kind of war that needs two hands is archery.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says about יהודה: 'His hands shall fight for him.' Which kind of fighting needs two hands? You have to say: this is the bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hint is in משה's ברכה to יהודה. 'Hands' in the plural points to fighting with a bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'ידיו', both hands, are fighting for יהודה. A sword can be held in one hand, but shooting a bow needs both hands, one to hold the bow and one to pull the string. So the ברכה hints that יהודה will use the bow.

keyTerms.meaning: His hands shall fight for him (from משה's ברכה to יהודה)
You must say, it must be

phrases.english: 'His hands shall contend for him.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7, from משה's ברכה to יהודה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא מִלְחָמָה שֶׁצְּרִיכָה שְׁתֵּי יָדַיִם?
phrases.english: And which kind of warfare needs two hands?
You must say: this is the bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 by finding the hint in דברים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ידיו רב לו' (two hands) hints at archery, which needs both hands.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: ספר הישר is שופטים
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says ספר הישר is ספר שופטים, because it says there 'each man did what was ישר in his own eyes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: ספר הישר is the book of שופטים. Why is it called 'the book of the upright'? Because it says: 'In those days there was no king in ישראל; each man did what was upright in his own eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion. רבי שמואל בר נחמני says ספר הישר is ספר שופטים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the others, he ties the name 'ישר' to a פסוק that uses that word. Here the פסוק in שופטים says each person did what was 'הישר' in his own eyes. Now there are three opinions: בראשית, דברים, and שופטים.

keyTerms.meaning: There was no king in ישראל

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: זֶה סֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said: this is the book of Judges,
and why did they call it 'the book of the upright'?
As it is written: 'In those days there was no king in Israel;'
'each man would do what was upright in his own eyes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: זֶה סֵפֶר שׁוֹפְטִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 20, different from רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ספר הישר is ספר שופטים, called 'ישר' because of the פסוק 'איש הישר בעיניו יעשה'.

steps.title: Where does שופטים hint at the bow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where ספר שופטים hints at teaching the bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where is it hinted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי שמואל בר נחמני's view the same test. Where does שופטים talk about teaching the bow?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion must show a hint in its book to teaching the bow, because the פסוק in שמואל ב says that teaching is written in ספר הישר. The same short question 'והיכא רמיזא' repeats for each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: The book of the upright, named in שמואל ב
The people of the tribe of יהודה

phrases.english: And where is it hinted?
phrases.notes: This time he means: where in שופטים is the bow hinted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source in שופטים that would back up רבי שמואל בר נחמני.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A hint in ספר שופטים to teaching the bow.

steps.title: 'To teach them war' means the bow
steps.stepSummary: שופטים says ה׳ left nations so that ישראל would learn war. The kind of war that needs to be learned is archery.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says: 'So that the generations of בני ישראל would know, to teach them war.' Which kind of fighting needs to be taught? You have to say: this is the bow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the hint is a פסוק in שופטים about teaching war. War that needs real training is shooting a bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'teaching' war. Simple fighting does not need lessons, but archery is a skill that has to be learned. So 'teaching war' hints at the bow.

phrases.english: 'So that the generations of the children of Israel would know,'
'to teach them war.'
And which kind of warfare needs learning?
You must say: this is the bow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 with a פסוק in שופטים about teaching war.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ללמדם מלחמה' refers to archery, the kind of war that needs training.

steps.title: How do we know this פסוק is about יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in שופטים speaks about all בני ישראל. The גמרא asks how we know it is about יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that it is written about יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spots a gap in the answer. The פסוק says 'בני ישראל', but the פסוק in שמואל ב is about teaching בני יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To match the פסוק in שמואל ב, the hint must be about יהודה specifically. 'ללמדם מלחמה' seems to be about everyone, so the גמרא wants proof that יהודה is meant.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that it is written about Judah?
phrases.notes: The פסוק just quoted says 'בני ישראל', so how do we know it means יהודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the hint from step 29 really fits יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the פסוק about teaching war in שופטים refers to יהודה.

steps.title: ה׳ chose יהודה to lead the fighting
steps.stepSummary: At the start of שופטים, ישראל ask who will go up first to fight the Canaanites, and ה׳ answers 'יהודה will go up'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it says: 'Who will go up for us first against the Canaanites to fight them? And ה׳ said: יהודה will go up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the opening of ספר שופטים. There, ה׳ picks יהודה to lead ישראל in war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר שופטים opens by making יהודה the tribe that leads the fighting. So when the same book talks about teaching war, it fits יהודה most of all. This links the hint back to 'teaching בני יהודה the bow'.
steps.whatToRemember: Three opinions on ספר הישר: רבי יוחנן says בראשית (the אבות), רבי אלעזר says דברים, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני says שופטים. Each explains the name 'ישר' and finds a hint to the bow.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'Who will go up for us first'
'against the Canaanites, to fight against them?'
'And the Lord said: Judah shall go up.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי יַעֲלֶה לָּנוּ בַתְּחִלָּה אֶל הַכְּנַעֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 30 by showing that in שופטים, יהודה leads the wars.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שופטים opens with ה׳ choosing יהודה to fight first, so the war-teaching in that book refers to יהודה.

steps.title: What does 'והעליה' mean in the פסוק about שאול's meal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where the cook brings שאול the thigh 'והעליה' and asks what 'והעליה' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it, and placed it before שאול.' What does 'והעליה' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes a פסוק in שמואל א and asks what the unclear word 'והעליה' refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'והעליה' seems to mean 'and what was on it', but it does not say what that was. The גמרא wants to know exactly which part of the animal was served to שאול.
steps.confusionAlert: Here שוק means the thigh of an animal, not a market.

phrases.english: 'And the cook lifted up the thigh and what was on it,'
'and placed it before Saul.'
What is 'and what was on it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the ספר הישר discussion and opens a new question about a word in a פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'והעליה' in שמואל א 9:24.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the thigh and the tail
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says 'והעליה' means the cook served the thigh together with the tail.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: the thigh and the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the part 'on' the thigh was the tail (אליה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'והעליה' as pointing to the אליה, the fatty tail of the sheep. So שאול was served two pieces together, the thigh and the tail.

keyTerms.meaning: The fatty tail of a sheep

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan says: the thigh and the tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והעליה' is the tail, served with the thigh.

steps.title: Why is the tail called 'what was on it'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, according to רבי יוחנן, the tail is described with the word 'והעליה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does it say 'and what was on it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up on רבי יוחנן's answer. If it means the tail, why describe it as 'on' the thigh?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'the tail'. The גמרא wants to know why the word 'on it' is used for the tail.

phrases.english: Why 'and what was on it'?
phrases.notes: Same words as before, but now he asks why the tail gets this name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind רבי יוחנן's reading in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the tail is described as being 'on' the thigh.

steps.title: The thigh holds up the tail
steps.stepSummary: The tail is called 'what is on it' because it rests on the thigh, which supports it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the thigh supports the tail.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the tail sits on top of the thigh, so it is 'what was on it'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the animal's body the tail leans on the thigh, and the thigh holds it up. That is why the פסוק calls the tail 'והעליה', the thing on the thigh.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן reads 'והעליה' as the tail, which rests on the thigh, so שאול was served the thigh and tail together.

phrases.english: Because the thigh supports the tail.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tail rests on the thigh, so it is called 'what was on it'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: The Thigh and the Breast
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the cook served שאול the thigh together with the breast. The breast is called 'what is on it' because it is placed on the thigh during the waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: it was the thigh and the breast. Why is the breast called 'what is on it'? Because when the meat needs to be waved, the breast is put on top of the thigh, and then it is waved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the question of what 'והעליה' means. רבי אלעזר says it is the breast, and the גמרא explains why the breast is called 'what is on it'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said 'what is on it' was the tail, which rests on the thigh. רבי אלעזר says it was the breast. It is 'on' the thigh because when these parts are waved, the breast is placed on top of the thigh. So the word 'on' comes from how the parts are handled during תנופה, not from where they sit on the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Waving: the sacrificial motion done with certain parts

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
It was the thigh and the breast.
Why is it called 'and what was on it'?
phrases.notes: The words come from שמואל א 9:24, where the cook lifts up the thigh 'and what was on it' for שאול.

phrases.english: Because one places the breast
on top of the thigh
when it needs to be waved,
and they wave it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation of 'והעליה', different from רבי יוחנן's thigh and tail.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והעליה' is the breast, which is placed on the thigh during the waving.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: The Thigh and the Top Cap
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the cook served the thigh together with the 'שופי', the top cap of the leg. It is called 'what is on it' because it sits right above the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says: it was the thigh and the שופי. Why is it called 'what is on it'? Because the שופי stands right above the thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third answer to what 'והעליה' means. As with רבי אלעזר, the גמרא asks why the word 'on it' fits and explains it according to his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reading is the most literal of the three: the שופי is physically the piece just above the thigh on the animal. So now there are three views of the extra part: the tail (רבי יוחנן), the breast (רבי אלעזר), or the שופי (רבי שמואל בר נחמני).

keyTerms.meaning: The cap: the very top part of the leg

steps.whatToRemember: Three readings of 'והעליה': the tail (רבי יוחנן), the breast placed on the thigh for waving (רבי אלעזר), and the top cap of the leg (רבי שמואל בר נחמני).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said:
It was the thigh and the cap.
Why is it called 'and what was on it'?
Because the cap stands on top of the thigh.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: שׁוֹק וְשׁוֹפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third explanation of 'והעליה' and closes this side discussion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'והעליה' is the שופי, the top of the leg, which sits right above the thigh.

steps.title: What Case Does the Rule About Being Alone With גוים Mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's rule that a woman may not be alone with גוים and asks what exact case the משנה is talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: a woman may not be alone with them. What case are we dealing with?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule about a woman being alone with גוים and asks what situation it means. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'לא תתייחד אשה עמהם' does not say how many people are there. By asking 'במאי עסקינן', the גמרא is getting ready to test each possible case. It will show that the simple reading makes the rule seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: She may not be alone (in seclusion)
Seclusion: a man and a woman being alone together
What case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: 'A woman may not be alone with them.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה earlier in the perek. 'Them' means גוים.

phrases.english: What case are we dealing with?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תִּתְיַיחֵד אִשָּׁה עִמָּהֶם, בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about שאול's portion and goes back to the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many גוים is the משנה's ban on a woman being alone with them talking about?

steps.title: If It Means One גוי, That Is Obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the משנה means one גוי, why say it? Even with a Jew it is forbidden, since a משנה teaches that one man may not be alone even with two women.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the משנה means alone with one גוי, would that be allowed even with a Jew? But we learned in a משנה: one man may not be alone with two women!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possible case, one גוי, and attacks it. It quotes a משנה showing that being alone with one man is already forbidden even when he is a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is: a woman alone with one Jewish man is forbidden. We know this because one man may not even be alone with two women, so one man with one woman is surely forbidden. So if our משנה only meant one גוי, it would be teaching something obvious. That suggests the משנה must mean a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (trying out a possible reading)
Is it permitted? (asked to mean: of course not)

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted משנה talks about one man with TWO women. The גמרא's point is 'all the more so': if even two women are not allowed, one woman with one man is surely forbidden.

phrases.english: If you say it means with one gentile,
is the same case permitted with a Jew?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא יִתְיַיחֵד אִישׁ אֶחָד עִם שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים״!
phrases.english: 'One man may not be alone with two women'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא בְּחַד, דִּכְוָותַהּ גַּבֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question of step 38 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה forbids a woman to be alone with one גוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being alone with one man is already forbidden even when he is a Jew, since one man may not be alone even with two women. So a special rule for one גוי would teach nothing new.
